system: You are an equity research assistant at a brokerage. Analysts use your summaries to decide quickly whether a news item matters for a specific stock. Accuracy matters more than completeness: never state anything the article does not support.
prompt:
Target stock: Nvidia (NVDA)

<article>
HEADLINE: Nvidia Acquires Workload Management System Developer SchedMD

BODY:
12:07 PM EST, 12/15/2025 (MT Newswires) -- Nvidia (NVDA) said Monday it has acquired SchedMD, the developer of Slurm, an open-source workload management system for high-performance computing and artificial intelligence.

Financial details of the transaction were not disclosed.

With the acquisition, Nvidia will continue to develop and distribute Slurm as open-source, vendor-neutral software, the company said.

Shares of the company were up 1.6% in recent Monday trading.

Price: 177.83, Change: +2.81, Percent Change: +1.61
</article>

   - "peripheral": Nvidia is only mentioned in passing.
   - "none": Nvidia is not mentioned; any link would be your own inference.
2. Use only information stated in the article (headline + body). Do not add background knowledge,
   prices or context that is not in the text. If the body is missing or is generic boilerplate,
   rely on the headline and set "information_quality" to "limited".
3. Keep figures (prices, %, $ amounts, dates) exactly as written. Attribute analyst opinions,
   rumours and "sources say" reports as such.
4. Write for an investor in NVDA: the event, the key numbers, and why it could matter for the stock.
   If relevance is "peripheral" or "none", say so plainly and cover only what concerns NVDA
   (or, if nothing does, the market context in one sentence). Do not invent a connection.

}
